mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of expected earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day period of similar rate levels (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically different from the 20-day forward return prior to the trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.2% inflation-adjusted growth for two consecutive months indicates accelerating demand for goods and services, which elevates earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the identified growth pattern (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in consumer confidence index (HOUST) suggests shifting supply constraints and improved sentiment, jointly increasing the probability of earnings beat expectations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month while HOUST increases by > 10 points
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative when sentiment (HOUST) is above 1400 (subjective threshold).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains unchanged at 5.25% for four consecutive months during a recessionary phase (as measured by GDP growth < -1%), the reduced policy rate uncertainty supports risk-on sentiment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS = 5.25% for 4 consecutive months and GDP growth < -1%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the policy stability (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in job openings (RSAFS) while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 4% indicates a cooling labor market, which can trigger a risk-off reaction and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day period of similar labor market conditions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained positive divergence between S&P 500 1-month forward implied volatility (not directly observable in the provided proxies) and the 10-year Treasury yield (not directly observable) would typically signal risk-appeal, but since only observable proxies are allowed, this sketch instead uses a proxy: when monthly industrial production (INDPRO) crosses above 105 (a historical high) during a rising inflation period (CPIAUCSL monthly > 0.3%), it predicts positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 105 and CPIAUCSL monthly > 0.3%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the cross and inflation signal (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a persistent rise in the 10-year yield proxy (not directly observable; using FEDFUNDS as a stand-in), if FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% month-over-month for three months in a row, it suggests higher real rates, which typically suppress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% each month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 5-day window (p > 0.05).
